subject: Draft Order Form: notice windows, grace period & termination language
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightscale.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@brightscale.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightScale draft order form - notice & termination redlines

Hi Tessa / Karthik —

Thanks for sending over the draft order form. We reviewed it with our procurement and legal teams and attached a redline with a couple of asks we consider material for our procurement policy. Key items in the attached BrightScale_OrderForm_Redlines.docx: 

- Auto-renew: we need the renewal term to be annual with a 60-day auto-renew window and a clear opt-out process.
- Notice window: request a 60-day written notice for non-renewal (aligning with our financial planning cycle).
- Termination for convenience: we propose a 60-day termination-for-convenience right with no early-termination fee for pilots, and a limited termination fee (equal to 25% of remaining committed monthly fees) for multi-year reserved capacity.
- Pilot exception: if we mark SKUs as "pilot" on the order form, those should be cancellable with 30 days' notice.

We tried to be pragmatic and flagged where the MSA and order form overlap. Can Redwood legal propose alternative wording that preserves your billing cadence but gives us predictability?

Suggested next step: a short sync (30 minutes) tomorrow to align on compromise language. Our procurement lead (procurements@brightscale.com) can join.

Attachments: BrightScale_OrderForm_Redlines.docx (redline)

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Procurement, BrightScale
elena@brightscale.com

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightscale.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightScale draft order form - notice & termination redlines

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the annotated redlines. Received and read.

High-level response before we loop legal in:
- We generally accept annual auto-renew but want to keep a 30–45 day opt-out window by default so we can make system and billing changes without breaking customers.
- Termination for convenience is fine in principle but we need to protect reserved capacity commitments for Dedicated tiers — we usually limit termination fees to a portion of committed months to cover provisioning.
- Pilot SKUs: happy to agree to a 30-day cancel for clearly identified pilots.

Karthik / Rishi — can you please: 
1) Propose concrete redline language for the MSA + order form that (a) gives BrightScale the predictability they want for renewals/notice windows, and (b) preserves Redwood's ability to recover reasonable provisioning costs for reserved capacity?
2) Flag any material legal or accounting impacts if we accept a 60-day universal notice (billing cutoff, pro-rata calculations, refund mechanics).

Elena — if you have availability, let's do a 30-min call tomorrow at 10:00 PT. If that doesn't work, propose two windows and we'll adjust.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(t) 415-555-0183

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@brightscale.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightScale draft order form - notice & termination redlines

Tessa / Elena — I reviewed BrightScale's redlines and sketched counter language below (high level) and will attach a marked-up order form for clarity.

High-level positions we recommend: 
- Auto-renew / Opt-out window: compromise to a 45-day written notice prior to renewal date. Concrete clause: "Either party may elect not to renew by providing written notice no later than forty-five (45) days prior to the then-current Term expiration." This balances BrightScale's planning needs and Redwood's billing run schedule.

- Notice for non-renewal: mirror the 45-day window above in the order form and include a simple one-click opt-out procedure referenced in the Console/Account settings.

- Termination for convenience: allow mutual termination for convenience with sixty (60) days' written notice, subject to the following: (a) For Reserved/Dedicated SKUs, Customer shall pay an early termination amount equal to the lesser of (i) 25% of the remaining committed monthly fees or (ii) three (3) months' fees, to cover GPU provisioning costs; (b) Pilot SKUs (explicitly enumerated on the order form) are cancellable with thirty (30) days' notice with no termination fee.

- Billing mechanics: propose pro-rata final invoice through the effective termination date; refunds (if any) to be issued within 60 days after invoice finalization. We should call out the billing cutoff (e.g., 5 business days before month-end for month-aligned subscriptions) — ops needs to confirm exact cutoff.

Risks / asks from our side: 
- If BrightScale insists on a universal 60-day opt-out, billing ops will need a month of lead time to adjust cutovers for reserved pools. That translates to potential overlap charges for one billing cycle. We should reflect that in the termination fee carve.
- Need explicit definition for "Pilot SKU" to avoid abuse — suggest an appendix to the order form where both parties initial pilot SKUs at signing.

I'll attach a redlined order form (Redwood_Response_Redlines.docx) with inline suggestions. If you want me to join tomorrow's call, I can make 10:00 PT for 30 minutes.

-Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Jason Miller <jmiller@brightscale.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightscale.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, procurements@brightscale.com
Date: 2026-08-31T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightScale draft order form - notice & termination redlines

Tessa / Karthik — appreciate the quick read and proposed compromise. A few notes from BrightScale legal before the call: 

- 45 days is close, but procurement is a hard 60-day requirement for our renewals team. Can Redwood accept 60 days for annual renewals and 30 days for shorter pilot orders? If not in the final language, we need a way to opt into 60 days per order (we can flag it on the order form).
- Pilot SKU appendix sounds reasonable — we'll draft the initial appendix and share during the call.
- We accept the proposed termination fee for Dedicated SKUs as a floor as long as there is a cap (three months' fees is acceptable).

We can do the 30-minute call today at 2:00 PM PT or tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT; Elena and procurements prefer tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT. Please confirm and we'll send a calendar invite.

Attachments referenced: BrightScale_OrderForm_Redlines.docx
Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to finalize redline and send latest mark-up before the call.
- Agree pilot appendix draft.
- If both agree, proceed to DocuSign for order form + exhibit.

Thanks,
Jason Miller
Senior Counsel, BrightScale
jmiller@brightscale.com
